text:
ConocoPhillips rose 3.4% today as oil prices climbed sharply on escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. Iran escalated attacks in the Strait of Hormuz this week, a critical chokepoint for global oil shipments, pushing U.S. crude toward $102 a barrel and Brent crude to $110. For an oil producer like ConocoPhillips, higher oil prices directly lift profit margins on every barrel they sell.

The broader backdrop amplifies the pressure: tanker rates have surged so much that the true cost to deliver physical oil is roughly $38 per barrel higher than the spot price suggests, according to recent analysis. This supply-side tension—combined with Trump's stated reluctance to use nuclear weapons or ground troops, which reduces some downside risk to the market—has kept energy investors buying into the sector. The stock's 15.6% gain over two weeks reflects a consistent climb as these geopolitical risks have mounted.
